status: retained: four-lane recurrent-state stores and resident scalar decode
platform: Dedicated gfx1151 Strix Halo, Linux x86-64, Nix release. No power or clock changes.
artifact_reference: dflash2-rollback.json: artifacts.target_q4, target_q8 and draft_q4; unchanged files.
change: Four-lane groups transpose four float4 columns using XOR1/XOR2 and write 64 contiguous bytes per value row. The value-major recurrent-state layout, values, copied bytes and allocation are unchanged. Loads remain unchanged.

Scalar temporaries avoid private storage from aggregate selections; inline-assembly register constraints bound exchange lifetimes. Retained output/state-only kernels use 227/203 VGPRs, 6/7 waves per SIMD and zero private storage. Float4 aggregate variants allocate 96 private bytes even when the compiler reports zero VGPR spills.

128x128 FP32 state now always uses the resident recurrence kernel, including scalar output. Scalar and verification arithmetic remain equivalent to the pinned generic kernel in the full-state/output probes. BF16 state and other dimensions retain the generic path.

The maintained recurrence ablation updates its one-row verification dispatch and keeps the generic operator control. No new maintained tool/test executable, sampling/controller changes or execution switch.

speed.method: Q4 target/Q4 draft, C1, greedy. Adaptive raw JSON/prose TG300: two timed samples per binary in ABBA order, 128-token raw prose warmup per binary excluded. Fixed-7 repetition chat TG128: two paired samples per binary in ABBA order. Includes prefill, excludes model loading. All IDs and acceptance statistics checked against qualified AR references. Candidate stores resident state through four-lane groups and enables resident FP32 scalar output for 128x128 shapes. Ordered arithmetic, state layout, draft, and controller are unchanged.

autoregressive.method: Q4 target, scalar AR, C1, pp2048/tg128, depth0, one benchmark repetition per invocation after built-in warmup. Four invocations in ABBA order; all128IDs must equal the fresh baseline and every repetition. Separate pp/tg rates from release gufo bench; no other depth or Q8 speed claim.

profile.method: One candidate prose TG300 diagnostic trace. Baseline reuses the immediately preceding qualified480bf3d trace from /tmp/qwen-replay-launch-release/profile.json. Identical Q4/Q4 artifacts, raw prompt, greedy adaptive controller, IDs and acceptance counts. GPU timings are attribution, not throughput.

microbenchmark.method: Final production template versus pinned480bf3d generic and resident kernels. FP32 48-head/16-key-head,128x128state. Eight successive updates with changing full-mantissa inputs compare every output/state bit before timing. Eight balanced rounds x192 launches, rotating48layers144MiB, identical state reset outside timing. Finalseed971; scalar four-lane precursor also passes seed19. Width1output compares the old scalar generic dispatcher; other widths and replay compare the old resident dispatcher.

paired_precursor.status: qualified but superseded by final four-lane implementation

speed.method: Q4 target/Q4 draft, C1, greedy. Adaptive raw JSON/prose TG300: two timed samples per binary in ABBA order, 128-token raw prose warmup per binary excluded. Fixed-7 repetition chat TG128: two paired samples per binary in ABBA order. Includes prefill, excludes model loading. All IDs and acceptance statistics checked against qualified AR references. Candidate stores resident state through adjacent lane pairs and enables resident FP32 scalar output for128x128shapes. Ordered arithmetic, state layout, draft, and controller are unchanged.

ar.method: Q4 target, scalar AR, C1, pp2048/tg128, depth0, one benchmark repetition per invocation after built-in warmup. Four invocations in ABBA order; all128IDs must equal the fresh baseline and every repetition. Separate pp/tg rates from release gufo bench; no other depth or Q8 speed claim.

profile.method: One candidate prose TG300 diagnostic trace. Baseline reuses the immediately preceding qualified480bf3d trace from /tmp/qwen-replay-launch-release/profile.json. Identical Q4/Q4 artifacts, raw prompt, greedy adaptive controller, IDs and acceptance counts. GPU timings are attribution, not throughput.

limits: Fresh short ABBA controls, two samples per binary/workload. DFlash2 prose/JSON/repetition include prefill and exclude loading. AR separately measures pp2048/tg128 at depth0. No full depth sweep, Q8 speed refresh or confidence-interval claim.

The diagnostic profile reuses the immediately preceding qualified 480bf3d trace as baseline and profiles only the candidate. Same prompt, IDs, acceptance, 5280 output and 4800 replay recurrence calls; use fresh unprofiled timings for total throughput.

Verification, cache and replay model checks compare against current AR; the pinned generic operator probes compare all state/output bits against 480bf3d. All 12 DFlash2 continuations retain qualified AR hashes; four fresh AR runs retain all 128 baseline IDs. Unchanged draft operator/sampling/HTTP/depth suites were not repeated.

Q4/Q8 target full-logit, feature, cache, rollback, replay and logical 262144 short-prefix controls passed. Prefill metrics are identical to the preceding qualified build. The SSM suite covers FP32/BF16.

Independent original checkpoint/conversion and MTP quality qualification, the complete speed matrix and C>1 serving throughput remain separate open work. The 75-question capability comparison has not run.
The original FP4 headline 65.6 JSON/26.1 prose decode-only remains unmatched; matched-Kquant results and the everyday 55 figure do not replace the goal.

Paired speed measurements and the candidate profile precede the rebase onto main b14316c. Model, sampler and kernel subtrees were unchanged by the rebase. The final integrated release has a separate fingerprint and passes affected unit/model/serving tests and one bounded continuation per workload; these controls are not a new paired speed estimate.

rebase.conflict_resolution: Preserve sampled draft_artifact_id scheme from main and Qwen draft_state_layout v3 plus versioned adaptive draft policy from branch; later branch commits replayed normally.

post_rebase_controls.method: Post-rebase bounded release controls: Q4/Q4, one candidate run each, no new speed sweep or paired estimate. Preserve every qualified AR token hash and acceptance/round count after main serving identity changes. GPU/model/sampler subtrees were unchanged by the rebase.

post_rebase_integration.serving_fixture_link_fix: Link the existing logger into the Qwen serving fixture: main's artifact fingerprinting now logs errors. The initial post-rebase fixture link failed with an undefined Logger::Log; after adding logging.cpp, the fixture and all bounded integration checks passed.

remaining_bottleneck.method: Sum candidate diagnostic GPU time for kernel names containing GEMM/GEMV, case-insensitive; includes target and draft matrix projections. This is profile attribution, not an end-to-end speed estimate.
